description: Backend-neutral maneuvers for the dynamic-v1 default. Reference values are MEASURED/published external figures with citations — never fitted from the run under test. Legacy kinematic-v1 traces are replayed under their recorded provenance and are not relabeled.

citations.title: FMVSS No. 135, Hydraulic and Electric Brake Systems (S5.1): a passenger car must stop from 62 mph (100 km/h) within 230 ft (70.1 m) on the prescribed surface
Euro NCAP AEB Car-to-Car Test Protocol v4.2 — CCRb lead-vehicle decelerations of 0.2–0.6 g; assessed vehicles deliver dry-pavement emergency deceleration of roughly 0.8–1.0 g (0.90 g nominal)
US NCAP request for comment (Federal Register, 2015-11-05) — lead-vehicle braking tests at 50/50 km/h with lead deceleration 0.2–0.6 g (2–6 m/s²)

Skid-pad lateral-grip compendium: typical passenger cars pull 0.7–0.9 g; family sedans about 0.7–0.8 g, sports cars 0.85–1.0 g; measured SUV/crossover examples 0.85–0.92 g (Porsche Macan 0.92 g, Audi SQ5 0.88 g, BMW X4 0.85 g)

SAE J1263 / J2263 road-load coastdown measurement; typical passenger-car road-load coefficients (Cd ≈ 0.30 with ≈ 2.2 m² frontal area, Crr ≈ 0.012) give a coastdown deceleration of ≈ 0.25 m/s² at 80 km/h for a 1500 kg vehicle
Mainstream sedan/SUV 0–100 km/h acceleration times cluster around 6–10 s depending on engine and mass; the mid-band figure used here is 8.5 s

references.note: mid-band of the mainstream 6–10 s cluster

references.derivation: v²/(2a_eff) with v = 100/3.6 m/s and a_eff = 8.0 m/s² mean deceleration — a 0.90 g dry-pavement capability less the jerk-limited onset/transient allowance of a real pedal or AEB ramp

references.note: generic passenger-car class sits in the lower half of the published 0.70–0.86 g family-sedan skidpad band
